findings.title: Test pins CatBoost classifier training-time predict() returning positive-class PROBABILITY — the exact semantics that diverge from the hard-label scored 'prediction' (catalog bug #24)
findings.description: catalog.md bug #24 (executed-repro, confirmed-real) documents that CatBoostAlgorithm.predict returns predict_proba[:,1] (a probability) during training diagnostics, while the scored/deployed 'prediction' column is the HARD class label (0/1); the same model's 'prediction' therefore means two different things, and residuals_histogram/actual_vs_predicted are computed as (label - probability). This test asserts exactly that buggy behaviour as intended: it feeds a classifier whose predict_proba returns [[0.8,0.2],[0.3,0.7],[0.5,0.5]] and asserts algo.predict(...) == [0.2, 0.7, 0.5] (the probabilities), with the docstring 'Classification model uses predict_proba and extracts column 1' framing the proba-return as correct. There is no test anywhere asserting that the training-time y_pred and the scored 'prediction' carry identical semantics for a given task (grep for predict_proba/hard_label/residual in test_modelling.py returns nothing). So when bug #24 is fixed (catalog's preferred fix: make scored 'prediction' the probability, or expose hard label as a derived column, and document the invariant), this test must be updated alongside.
findings.evidence: Source confirms the mechanics: src/haute/modelling/_algorithms.py:610-611 `if isinstance(model, CatBoostClassifier): preds = model.predict_proba(x_data)[:, 1]`. Training feeds it to diagnostics: _training_job.py:1136 `y_pred = algo.predict(model, diag_df, features)` then :1217 `compute_residuals_histogram(y_true, y_pred, w)` / :1218 `compute_actual_vs_predicted(y_true, y_pred, w)`. The test asserts `np.testing.assert_array_almost_equal(preds, [0.2, 0.7, 0.5])` — i.e. the probability, not the hard label the scorer writes (catalog #24: ScoringModel.predict -> model.predict returns 0/1).
findings.recommended_fix: When fixing catalog bug #24, change this test to assert the chosen consistent semantics and add a cross-surface invariant test: train a real CatBoostClassifier, run it through both the training diagnostic path (compute_residuals_histogram/actual_vs_predicted inputs) and the scoring path (_score_eager / _batch_score_to_parquet 'prediction' column), and assert the two 'prediction' surfaces carry identical semantics (both probability, or both hard label). Until the fix lands, at minimum rename the docstring to flag that this pins training-only semantics that intentionally differ from scored output, and reference bug #24.

findings.title: Suite codifies id(scoring_model)-keyed feature-validation cache as the intended contract — the id()-reuse footgun the catalog (bug #54) flags as latent-wrong and recommends removing
findings.description: catalog.md bug #54 (executed-repro, confirmed-real, severity low/latent) shows _validate_features keys on (id(scoring_model), contract_key, schema_key) and that transient ScoringModel carriers built in _score_batched_unified (and load_local_model deploy artifacts) are never registered in _model_cache, so the eviction cascade never fires for them; after GC, CPython can reuse a freed carrier's id() for a different ScoringModel with the same contract+schema and serve the stale validation result without re-validating. The catalog's recommended fix is to DROP id(scoring_model) from the key (the payload is a pure function of contract_key+schema) or key on a monotonic per-instance token. This test suite instead pins id()-keying as correct: test_different_scoring_model_instance_is_miss asserts two simultaneously-live distinct objects miss (true only because both are alive so ids differ) with the docstring stating 'Cache is keyed on id(scoring_model)', and TestAPIShape.test_required_symbols_exist mandates _invalidate_feature_validation_cache_for plus the entire eviction-cascade machinery the recommended fix would delete. Critically, NO test exercises the actual defect — an id reused after a transient carrier is GC'd colliding with a new model of the same contract+schema (the catalog's PART 2 repro). So the suite locks in the buggy design and is blind to its failure mode.
findings.evidence: catalog.md #54: 'Remove the latent footgun ... drop id(scoring_model) from the key entirely and rely on the contract key + schema key'. Repro PART 2 PROVEN: a distinct never-validated ScoringModel B served A's cached tuple with _validate_features_uncached NOT called for B. Test docstring (line 280): 'Cache is keyed on id(scoring_model) — the second object has a different Python identity'. test_cache_is_bounded_lru/test_required_symbols_exist pin _feature_validation_cache + _invalidate_feature_validation_cache_for as required API.
findings.recommended_fix: When fixing bug #54, replace test_different_scoring_model_instance_is_miss's id()-identity rationale with the content-key contract, and add a regression test that constructs two distinct ScoringModels sharing contract+schema and asserts the validator runs per-object (the catalog repro shape, using the permitted id monkeypatch shadowed inside _model_scorer) so an id-reuse collision can never silently cross-serve. If the cache is re-keyed purely on (contract_key, schema_key) per the catalog fix, delete the eviction-cascade API-shape assertions rather than leaving them pinning dead machinery.

findings.title: No test exercises source_type='run' with a non-empty version, so the V019 fast-path/canonical cache-key divergence (double-miss, orphaned cache entry, skewed hit/miss counters) is entirely unverified — while the observability suite asserts counter MONOTONICITY that V019 says is broken in production
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V019 (executed-repro, high) shows load_mlflow_model builds the fast-path key with version='' (_mlflow_io.py:893-900) but the canonical/slow-path key with resolved_version (:968-974); for source_type='run' resolve_mlflow_source returns resolved_version=version unchanged, and production ALWAYS passes version=config.get('version','latest') (_model_scorer.py:1248 -> 1019/1063). So a run-sourced catboost/rustystats model with version='latest' takes a 5-tuple canonical key that never matches the 4-tuple fast-path key: it loads from disk twice, leaves a permanently-orphaned duplicate cache entry, and double-counts misses; pyfunc loses the fast path entirely. Every test that touches the run fast/slow path omits version (defaults), so the divergence is never hit: TestLoadMlflowModelFastCache hardcodes the 4-tuple ('run','abc123','model.cbm','regression') (lines 1643,1685,1692, with comment 'Key uses resolved version "" for run-based'), TestModelCache (lines 226-271) likewise, and the ENTIRE test_model_cache_observability suite drives _primed_load with no version. That observability suite asserts exactly the counters V019 breaks: test_misses_monotonic_over_distinct_loads expects 5 distinct loads => +5 misses, test_hit_counter_increments_on_repeat_load expects a repeat => +1 hit. Under the real production call shape (version='latest') a run model would miss twice on first load and the repeat would still miss (slow-key path) — non-monotonic — yet no test covers it. The grep confirms the only run+version-ish coverage is registered-source (test_mlflow_io.py:142 version='2'; concurrency:455-499 version='7'), never run+version.
findings.evidence: _mlflow_io.py:894-900 fast_key uses `version=""`; :968-974 cache_key uses `version=resolved_version`; _model_cache_key (:311-313) returns 5-tuple when version truthy else 4-tuple. _model_scorer.py:1248 `version=cfg.get("version", "latest")`. test_model_cache_observability.py _primed_load passes source_type='run', run_id, artifact_path, task — no version. test_mlflow_io.py:1692 comment 'Key uses resolved version "" for run-based'. Grep for version= in test_mlflow_io.py returns only line 142 (registered). VERIFIED-BUGS V019 repro V019.py confirms the duplicate orphaned entry and skewed counters.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a failing regression test (TDD) that calls load_mlflow_model(source_type='run', run_id=..., artifact_path='model.cbm', version='latest', task='regression') twice and asserts: (a) exactly ONE entry lands in _model_cache for that run/artifact, (b) get_model_cache_stats() shows misses==1, hits==1 after the second call (not misses==2/3), (c) the second call does not re-invoke _load_catboost_model. Mirror it for pyfunc. This test fails today and pins the V019 fix (collapse the run-source key to the 4-tuple on both paths). Also add a version='latest' variant to test_misses_monotonic_over_distinct_loads so the observability suite reflects the real production call shape.

findings.location: tests/test_model_explainability.py:330-516 (_FakeRustyStatsGLM tests) — no test for missing/None required GLM field
findings.title: No test asserts that a GLM contribution record MISSING (or None) a required numeric field raises ModelExplanationError — V028's silent-accept path is uncovered, and the suite only ever feeds fully-populated records
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V028 (executed-repro, high) shows _assert_finite_glm_record validates required fields via _as_float(record.get(field), strict=True) and discards the result, but _as_float short-circuits None -> returns None BEFORE the strict branch (_model_explainability.py:25-26). So a record that is MISSING base_value/sum_contributions/prediction_from_contributions/prediction_value (or carries explicit None) passes _assert_finite_glm_record silently; the only thing that later catches it is the additivity reconstruction check (a bare assert under -O is stripped). Every explainability test that exercises _assert_finite_glm_record supplies ALL four required numeric fields with finite values (lines 378-381, 442-445, 469-472, 498-501, 639-642). There is a test for additivity-break (test_..._when_additivity_breaks, line 490, sets prediction_from_contributions=99.0) and for prediction mismatch (line 461) and missing FEATURES (line 434), but NONE for a missing/None required numeric field. Given CLAUDE.md's fail-loud mandate and that this validator exists precisely to make malformed records loud, the absence of a test on the None/missing path is a critical-path coverage gap on a pricing-explainability surface.
findings.evidence: _model_explainability.py:25-26 `if value is None: return None` (before the strict raise at :32/:36); :317-318 `_as_float(record.get(field), field_name=field, strict=True)` (result discarded). Tests grep: every base_value/sum_contributions/prediction_from_contributions appears with a numeric literal; no record omits a required field or sets it to None. VERIFIED-BUGS V028 repro V028.py confirms a missing-field record passes and only a bare assert (or downstream) would catch it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add tests (TDD, will fail until V028 fix) feeding _FakeRustyStatsGLM a record that (a) omits 'base_value' entirely and (b) sets 'sum_contributions' to None, and assert explain_rustystats_prediction raises ModelExplanationError naming the offending field — for each of the four required fields and for a None 'contributions[i].contribution'. The paired production fix is an explicit `is None` rejection in _assert_finite_glm_record (or making _as_float(strict=True) reject None).

findings.title: GLM coefficients_table / relativities tests assert only key-presence and relativity>0 — they never check that each coefficient/relativity maps to the CORRECT feature, so the name/coef misalignment fabrication (catalog bug #53) is uncaught
findings.description: catalog.md bug #53 (executed-repro, confirmed-real) shows the GLM coefficient/relativity fallbacks guard only on array LENGTH (_rustystats.py:106-109 _align_coefs_and_names checks `len(coefs) > len(names)`; coefficients_table checks shortest<len(coefs)), never on name/coef ordering or intercept identity — so a model whose coefficients are mis-ordered relative to feature_names silently attaches every relativity/coefficient to the WRONG feature label (repro: F1<->F2 relativity swap 7.3891 vs 1.0). The unit tests for these methods are tautological/weak: test_coefficients_table only asserts len(table)>0 and that the dict has keys 'feature'/'coefficient'/'p_value' (never that a known feature has its known coefficient); test_relativities only asserts len(rels)>0, presence of 'feature'/'relativity', and relativity>0 (which is trivially true for any exp(coef)). Neither pins the feature->coefficient correspondence that bug #53 corrupts. (The adjacent test_coefficients_table_deserialized_model_fails_loud at line 438 is good and covers the SE=0/p=1 fabrication trigger, but not the ordering misalignment.)
findings.evidence: _rustystats.py:106-109 `if len(coefs) > len(names): names = ['(Intercept)'] + names; min_len = min(len(coefs), len(names)); return coefs[:min_len], names[:min_len]` — length-only. test_coefficients_table asserts only `'feature' in first`, `'coefficient' in first`, `'p_value' in first`. test_relativities asserts only `'feature' in first`, `'relativity' in first`, `first['relativity'] > 0`. catalog #53 repro modelling__glm-relativities-coef-ordering-fabrication-boundary.py demonstrates the silent swap with no exception.
findings.recommended_fix: Strengthen these tests to fit a GLM with known, distinguishable per-feature effects (e.g. one strongly positive term, one ~zero term) and assert the SPECIFIC coefficient/relativity attaches to the SPECIFIC feature name (e.g. table['driver_age'].coefficient is within tolerance of the fitted value and != area's). Add a fabrication-boundary regression mirroring catalog #53: stub a model whose coefficients/feature_names are mis-ordered (equal length) and assert coefficients_table/relativities raise rather than silently relabel — pinning the bug #53 fix (validate name/coef alignment, not just length).

findings.title: Proba-helper tests assert 'no exception / column appears' for over-mocked MagicMock models rather than verifying the binary-positive-class contract end to end
findings.description: Several TestAppendClassificationProba cases lean on MagicMock predict_proba return values and assert only that a '<col>_proba' column is present (or absent), not the labeling correctness. test_regression_should_not_call_this is explicitly tautological — its own body comment says 'the helper itself doesn't check task, it just appends probas' and it asserts the column appears, which validates nothing about behaviour the caller relies on. test_no_predict_proba_returns_unchanged asserts result.equals(df) for a MagicMock(spec=[]) — fine as far as it goes but it is a shape/identity check. These are low-value compared to the strong real-model tests immediately below (TestAppendClassificationProbaShapes / TestEagerBatchProbaAgreement at lines 761-931) which DO drive REAL CatBoost models and assert eager==batch and multiclass-raises; those are the meaningful tests. The weak ones add cost and risk masking a future regression (e.g. a MagicMock will happily return a 2D array even if the production model contract changed).
findings.evidence: Line 695-705 test_regression_should_not_call_this docstring: 'This test validates the contract: the helper itself doesn't check task' then `assert 'pred_proba' in result.columns`. Line 677-684 asserts `result.equals(df)` on MagicMock(spec=[]). Contrast the real-model agreement tests at 848-930 which use _train_real_catboost_classifier and np.testing.assert_array_equal across eager and batch.
findings.recommended_fix: Either delete test_regression_should_not_call_this (it asserts a non-contract) or convert it to assert the documented caller convention is enforced elsewhere. Keep the strong real-model shape/agreement tests. Prefer the real-CatBoost fixtures over MagicMock predict_proba for any test claiming to pin the proba labeling, so the binary positive-class contract is actually exercised.

findings.title: Cache-reset fixtures swallow all exceptions / use getattr-or-skip, which can let the suite pass when the production cache/clear API is absent or broken
findings.description: The observability autouse fixture wraps clear_model_cache() in `try: ... except Exception: pass` with a comment that a missing cache dir is fine; this broad except will also silently swallow a genuinely broken clear_model_cache (e.g. one that raises a real error), so a regression in the reset surface would not fail the suite and could leave stale counters that mask hit/miss assertions. Similarly test_feature_validation_cache's _clear_caches uses getattr(ms, '_clear_feature_validation_cache', None) and no-ops if absent — appropriate while the feature was xfail-staged, but now that the API is required (TestAPIShape asserts it exists), the silent no-op path is dead weight that could hide a half-reverted cache. These are fixtures, not assertions, but they weaken the determinism guarantee the counter-monotonicity tests depend on.
findings.evidence: test_model_cache_observability.py:48-55 `try: from haute._mlflow_io import clear_model_cache; clear_model_cache() except Exception: pass`. test_feature_validation_cache.py:112-114 `clear_fn = getattr(ms, '_clear_feature_validation_cache', None); if clear_fn is not None: clear_fn()`.
findings.recommended_fix: Narrow the observability fixture's except to the specific expected condition (e.g. catch only the missing-cache-dir case) so a broken clear_model_cache fails loudly. In test_feature_validation_cache, now that _clear_feature_validation_cache is a required symbol, call it directly (no getattr guard) so a regression that drops it fails the reset rather than silently no-op'ing.

findings.location: tests/test_explore_routes.py:785-908 (TestBuildFrameStats categorical value-count suite; no Binary case anywhere in file)
findings.title: No test exercises a Binary column in Explore; the verified strict-cast crash (V099) on non-UTF-8 bytes is entirely uncovered
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V099: src/haute/routes/_explore_service.py:331 _categorical_value_counts_expr does pl.col(name).cast(pl.String) (STRICT). Binary is in _TEXT_DTYPE_BASES (line 78), so _supports_categorical_value_counts(Binary) and _has_categorical_value_counts(Binary) are both True (lines 136-167), routing every Binary column through that strict cast inside the single batched streaming_collect that builds ALL frame stats (lines 445-454). A Binary column holding any non-UTF-8 byte sequence (hashes, serialized blobs, image bytes) raises ComputeError 'invalid utf8' and aborts the WHOLE Explore materialisation for the frame, not just that column. The explore test suite has extensive categorical coverage (String, Categorical, Boolean, Date, List-as-unsupported, count-named column) but ZERO Binary coverage (grep for Binary/non-UTF/0xff returns nothing). Notably test_build_frame_stats_keeps_unsupported_categorical_profiles_unexpanded (line 890) pins a List column (which is correctly unsupported, expandable=False), but never a Binary column (which IS 'supported' and thus hits the strict cast) — so the one negative-path test sits right next to the gap and misses it.
findings.evidence: Reproduced directly: `pl.Series('blob',[b'\xff\xfe',b'\x00\x01'],dtype=pl.Binary).to_frame().lazy().select(pl.col('blob').cast(pl.String).value_counts()).collect()` -> polars.exceptions.ComputeError: invalid utf8 (expression col("blob").strict_cast(String)). The non-strict form `.cast(pl.String, strict=False)` succeeds. Because _build_frame_stats batches every column's aggregations into one streaming_collect (line 450), one bad Binary column aborts stats for the entire frame.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a failing test (TDD for V099) to TestBuildFrameStats: build a LazyFrame with a Binary column containing non-UTF-8 bytes (e.g. b'\xff\xfe') plus a normal numeric column, call _build_frame_stats, and assert (a) it does NOT raise, (b) the numeric column's stats are still computed, and (c) the Binary column gets a 'Text' kind with invalid bytes surfaced as a null categorical bucket. This pins the V099 fix (cast(pl.String, strict=False)) and guards the whole-frame-abort regression. Also add an HTTP-level explore/run test with a Binary parquet column so the end-to-end materialisation path is covered.

findings.location: tests/test_pipeline_route_supersession.py:95-1517 (whole SupersessionCoordinator suite; none covers the both-tasks-done branch)
findings.title: Semaphore double-release / permit leak (V101) in _acquire_limiter_unless_superseded is untested despite an extensive supersession suite
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V101: in src/haute/routes/_supersession.py:182-196, when asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) returns with BOTH acquire_task and superseded_task in done (reachable whenever a permit is free at the same event-loop step the request is superseded), the just-acquired permit is released TWICE: once at line 184 (limiter.release(); acquired=False) before raising SupersededRequestError, then the except handler at 189-195 re-derives acquired=True from the drained acquire result (line 191-192, which has no memory that 184 already released) and releases again at 195. Net: Semaphore._value is incremented by one, permanently raising the per-key concurrency cap and defeating the bounded-worker guarantee. The supersession test file is ~1500 lines and very thorough about HTTP-level outcomes (status counts, call_count, max_active, slot lifecycle, timeouts), but NO test drives the both-done race or asserts on the limiter permit count after a superseded-while-permit-available acquire. The closest tests assert max_active<=cap under happy-path timing, which does not catch a leaked permit that only manifests on the specific same-step race.
findings.evidence: review/04-exhaustive/repro/V101.py drives the REAL private coroutine: a real asyncio.Semaphore(1) plus a _SupersessionState whose latest_generation (2) is ahead of the passed generation (1) makes _wait_until_superseded return without suspending while limiter.acquire() also returns immediately (permit free) -> asyncio.wait returns both tasks done. After one superseded acquire attempt, limiter._value goes 1 -> 2 (correct is 1), and a fresh Semaphore(1) then grants 2 back-to-back acquires with no release. Existing tests never construct this generation-ahead state.
findings.recommended_fix: Port V101.py into tests/test_pipeline_route_supersession.py as a failing regression: instantiate a SupersessionCoordinator + asyncio.Semaphore(1), set _SupersessionState.latest_generation ahead of the generation argument, await coordinator._acquire_limiter_unless_superseded(...), assert it raises SupersededRequestError AND that limiter._value == 1 (not 2), then assert exactly one back-to-back acquire succeeds. This pins the V101 fix (track permit ownership with a dedicated holds_permit flag, remove the resurrection at L191-192).

findings.title: train_status timeout arithmetic (V100) is only tested with a numeric timeout=10; a JSON-null/string timeout 500s and is uncovered
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V100: src/haute/routes/modelling.py:67-68 does `timeout = job.get('timeout', _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)` then `if start and (time.monotonic() - start) > timeout`. `timeout` originates from user job config and is not coerced; if it is JSON null or a string, the comparison raises TypeError -> 500. Every timeout test (test_timeout_sets_error_with_elapsed:541, test_completed_job_not_overwritten_by_timeout:583, and the start request at :437) injects the integer 10. No test sets timeout to None, a string, or a missing-but-running job that exercises a non-numeric value, so the TypeError path is entirely uncovered.
findings.evidence: Reproduced the arithmetic in isolation: with job={'status':'running','start_time': monotonic()-500,'timeout': None}, `(monotonic()-start) > timeout` raises `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'`; with timeout='30' it raises `TypeError ... 'float' and 'str'`. grep of test_modelling_routes.py shows the only timeout literals are `10` at lines 437, 541, 583.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a failing test that creates a running job with `timeout=None` (and a parametrised string variant) and asserts GET /api/modelling/train/status/{job_id} returns a clean terminal/error response (e.g. 400 contract error or a coerced default) rather than 500. Pin the V100 fix in modelling.py (validate/coerce job timeout to a positive number before the comparison, failing loudly on non-numeric config).

findings.title: No test applies two different online frontier points on one live job; the verified full-clear-of-heavy-state bug (V096) is uncovered
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V096: src/haute/routes/optimiser.py:1288 apply_lambdas calls `_store.clear_result_data(body.job_id)` with NO keys after a frontier-point apply, defaulting to the full _HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS set and wiping quote_grid/solver mid frontier-analysis session (every other frontier-session exit preserves heavy state via _clear_result_data_after_user_action while frontier points exist). Consequence: after applying online frontier point 0, applying a DIFFERENT point N (no cached frontier_apply_result:N artifact) re-enters _materialise_frontier_point_apply -> touch_heavy_objects(required_keys=('quote_grid',)) now returns False -> HTTP 400 'Quote grid is not available for this job.' test_apply_after_solve (4365) applies exactly once; test_apply_reuses_cached_frontier_apply_artifact_for_online_mode (594) deliberately pre-seeds a cached artifact so it never re-materialises; the frontier/select tests use a single point_index. No test does point-0 apply followed by point-N apply on the same in-memory job, so neither the correct symmetric behaviour nor the bug is pinned.
findings.evidence: review/04-exhaustive/repro/V096.py asserts the SECOND apply of a different valid frontier point returns HTTP 400 ('Quote grid is not available...') where a symmetric session would return 200, tracing the cause to the keyless clear_result_data at optimiser.py:1288 vs the frontier-aware clears used elsewhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a failing route test (TDD for V096): seed a completed frontier job with >=2 points and live heavy state (solver/quote_grid), POST /api/optimiser/apply {point_index:0} expecting 200, then POST /api/optimiser/apply {point_index:1} on the same job and assert 200 (not 400). Pin the fix that apply_lambdas must preserve quote_grid/solver while the job still has frontier points (use the frontier-aware clear), mirroring the other session exits.

findings.title: Concurrency test for atomic_update only asserts 'no exception + >=1 field present', codifying the documented lost-update behaviour as acceptable
findings.description: test_atomic_update_thread_safety runs 20 threads each writing a distinct field_{idx} but asserts only that no exception is raised, status is unchanged, and at least one field_N survived (len(field_keys) >= 1). Its own docstring states the read-modify-write `old = d[k]; d[k] = {**old, **fields}` is NOT linearisable and concurrent writers to different keys can lose each other's updates, declaring that acceptable for the real single-writer workload. This is honest but it pins a lossy behaviour as intended: a future change that made atomic_update genuinely merge all concurrent distinct-key writes would not be rewarded, and a regression that LOST MORE updates would not be caught (the assertion passes as long as one of 20 writes survives). The stronger linearisability properties are only covered for the same-status compare-and-swap (test_atomic_update_with_expected_status_is_optimistic_lock:657) and the heavy-present path (553), not for plain distinct-key concurrent merges.
findings.evidence: Lines 938-942: `assert result['status'] == 'running'; field_keys = [k for k in result if k.startswith('field_')]; assert len(field_keys) >= 1`. With 20 distinct keys submitted, this passes even if 19 updates are lost. The docstring (lines 909-919) explicitly accepts non-linearisable lost updates.
findings.recommended_fix: Either strengthen to assert all 20 distinct-key writes survive (if the store is intended to be safe for distinct-key concurrent writers — which would also pin a real correctness property), or, if the single-writer contract is deliberate, replace the multi-distinct-key scenario with one that asserts the actual invariant the production code relies on (single background writer + reader sees no torn state, as test_atomic_update_vs_reader_no_partial_state already does) so the test stops implying distinct-key merge safety that the code does not provide.

findings.title: Bundler tests codify the silent-skip of misconfigured modelScore nodes; no serve-side test pins the resulting null-prediction passthrough (verified bug V044)
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V044 (high): a modelScore node misconfigured so the bundler skips it entirely (no model AND no contract bundled) is served as a SILENT passthrough at deploy time — _scorer.py:_intercept's MODEL_SCORE branch finds remapped_path=None and bundled_contract_path=None, skips both guard branches, and hits `return None` (line 733), falling through to _build_model_score which passes the input through with no prediction. The fail-loud guard (model_score_missing_artifact, lines 681-704) only fires `if bundled_contract_path is not None`. The test suite codifies the bundler half of this bug as intended behaviour: test_model_score_skipped_without_run_id asserts a modelScore with `{'sourceType':'run'}` and no run_id yields `len(artifacts)==0`, and test_registered_model_skipped_without_model_name asserts the same for an empty registered_model. Because the bundler emits neither a model nor a contract for these nodes, they are exactly the precondition for V044's passthrough. test_deploy_scorer_artifact_cache.py:234-261 covers ONLY the contract-bundled-without-model branch (which correctly raises). There is NO test asserting that the neither-model-nor-contract case raises at serve time — and the bundler tests affirmatively pin the silent skip, so a reviewer reading the suite would conclude this is intended.
findings.evidence: test_deploy.py:322-323 `artifacts = collect_artifacts(graph, [], Path('.')); assert len(artifacts) == 0` for `config={'sourceType':'run'}` (no run_id). _scorer.py:677 `if bundled_contract_path is not None:` gates the only RuntimeError; with both None the code reaches `return None` at line 733 → passthrough. The only fail-loud test (test_deploy_scorer_artifact_cache.py:255 `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='model artifact')`) supplies `{f'ms__{CONTRACT_FILENAME}': str(contract_path)}` — a bundled contract, i.e. the OTHER branch.
findings.recommended_fix: When V044 is fixed (raise in _intercept when a configured-looking modelScore has neither remapped_path nor bundled_contract_path), add a serve-side regression test: build the _model_score_graph() with a real run_id/artifact_path config but pass artifact_paths={} (nothing bundled), call score_graph(...), and assert it raises RuntimeError naming the node rather than returning the input unchanged. Until then, the two bundler tests should be annotated (or paired with the serve-side assertion) to make clear that an unbundled modelScore must NOT be served as a passthrough — the current assertions silently bless the dangerous precondition.

findings.title: find_config_by_func_name traversal tests are vacuous: the only assertion is gated behind `if result is not None`, which never executes given the real guard
findings.description: The class TestFindConfigByFuncNameTraversal claims to verify that func_name path traversal is blocked. But src/haute/_config_io.py:297 rejects any func_name containing '..', '/' or '\\' by returning None. Both tests therefore ALWAYS take the `result is None` path and assert NOTHING. The body `if result is not None: ... assert config_data.get('leaked') is True` is dead code under current behaviour. These tests pass today, but they would also pass if the security guard were deleted entirely (the traversal would still resolve to a non-existent path under a different layout and return None), AND — far worse — they provide zero protection against a regression: if a future change made find_config_by_func_name return a non-None config for `../../secret`, the test would actively ASSERT that the leaked content is returned (asserting the vulnerability is 'working') rather than failing. A security test whose sole assertion fires only when the code is vulnerable is worse than no test: it inverts the intended contract.
findings.evidence: _config_io.py:297 `if '..' in func_name or '/' in func_name or '\\' in func_name: ... return None`. Test: `result = find_config_by_func_name('../../secret', base_dir=tmp_path); if result is not None: config_data, _ = result; assert config_data.get('leaked') is True` — the assertion is unreachable for the blocked input, so the test is a no-op.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the assertion unconditional and aligned with the contract: `assert find_config_by_func_name('../../secret', base_dir=tmp_path) is None` and `assert find_config_by_func_name('../model_scoring/victim', base_dir=tmp_path) is None`. Optionally also assert the warning log 'config_recovery_rejected' is emitted (via capture_logs) to pin that rejection — not mere absence — is the reason for None.

findings.title: Test named 'PathURLSchemeRejection' asserts that validate_safe_path does NOT reject URL schemes — the assertion contradicts the class/contract name
findings.description: The class docstring states 'validate_safe_path or read_source must reject paths starting with URL schemes.' The test test_url_scheme_in_validate_safe_path then asserts the OPPOSITE for validate_safe_path: for inputs like 'http://evil.com/data.csv' and 'file:///etc/shadow' it asserts `result.is_relative_to(tmp_path)` — i.e. that validate_safe_path silently TREATS the URL as a relative child path and returns it without rejection. I verified src/haute/routes/_helpers.py:78-102: validate_safe_path has no scheme check; it only blocks null bytes, absolute escapes and post-resolve escapes, so 'http://evil.com/...' becomes `(base / 'http:/evil.com/...').resolve()` inside base. The companion read_source test (lines 714-727) does enforce rejection, so the suite is not vacuous overall — but this specific assertion codifies a surprising behaviour (a URL-looking string passing the path validator) under a class name that promises rejection. A reader scanning for 'is URL-scheme rejection covered?' is actively misled, and if a future hardening adds scheme rejection to validate_safe_path, this test will fail spuriously and be 'fixed' by re-deleting the protection.
findings.evidence: _helpers.py:78-102 contains no URL-scheme handling. Test asserts `result.is_relative_to(tmp_path.resolve())` for scheme_path in {'http://evil.com/data.csv','https://...','ftp://...','file:///etc/shadow'} with the message 'URL-scheme path should resolve within base, not trigger external access'.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename/retarget the assertion to reflect the real defence boundary: the protection against SSRF lives in read_source (extension/scheme guard), not validate_safe_path. Either (a) split this into a clearly-named test 'validate_safe_path treats URL-looking strings as in-tree filenames (no fetch)' and keep the SSRF contract solely on the read_source test, or (b) if URL schemes SHOULD be rejected by validate_safe_path, change the assertion to `pytest.raises(HTTPException)` and fix the helper. As written, the class name overpromises while the body under-delivers.

findings.title: Dev-mode --port propagation to the Vite proxy is untested (verified bug V004): the test asserts only that npm is invoked
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V004: in dev mode --port is silently broken — the backend port is never propagated to the Vite dev server, whose proxy targets a hardcoded 127.0.0.1:8000 (frontend/vite.config.ts). The dev-mode test asserts ONLY that subprocess.Popen is called once with npm as argv[0]; it never inspects the child env (the `env=` kwarg) for any backend host/port, nor the displayed banner URLs. So a user running `haute serve --port 9000` in dev mode gets a frontend that proxies to the wrong backend, with zero test coverage of the regression. The non-dev test (lines 220-254) correctly checks uvicorn gets port 9000, which creates a false sense that --port is fully covered.
findings.evidence: test_cli_serve.py:279-290 asserts `mock_popen.assert_called_once()` and that the command basename starts with 'npm'; no assertion on `mock_popen.call_args.kwargs.get('env')`. VERIFIED-BUGS V004 fix note: 'propagate the backend bind to the Vite child via env (env["HAUTE_BACKEND_HOST"]=..., env["HAUTE_BACKEND_PORT"]=...)'.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test that invokes `serve --no-browser --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000` in dev mode and asserts the Vite child env carries the backend bind (e.g. `mock_popen.call_args.kwargs['env']['HAUTE_BACKEND_PORT'] == '9000'`) once V004 is fixed; as a RED test it currently demonstrates the missing propagation. Also assert the dev banner reflects the chosen port.

findings.title: In-flight admission: the first/single reservation exceeding (available_ram - os_reserve) is never tested (verified bug V029)
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V029: _reserve_in_flight_budget (src/haute/_execution_admission.py:507-523) refuses the FIRST admission when a single profile's memory LIMIT exceeds (available_ram - os_reserve), because the guard `if reserved + reservation_bytes > limit_bytes` has no clamp for the empty-ledger case. The existing test sets available_ram to a generous 10 GiB so the FIRST OPTIMISER_SETUP job is admitted, and only the SECOND concurrent job is rejected with reason='in_flight_memory_budget_exceeded'. It thus exercises the cumulative-ledger path but never the pathological single-job-too-big case (reserved==0 and reservation_bytes > limit_bytes), which is the actual defect: on a modest machine the very first/only heavy job is refused even with nothing else running. No test pins that a single reservation must always be admitted.
findings.evidence: _execution_admission.py:513 `if reserved + reservation_bytes > limit_bytes:` with reserved==0 reduces to `reservation_bytes > limit_bytes` and raises. Test monkeypatches available_ram to 10*gib (line 269-270) so the first job fits; assertion at line 284 only covers the second job rejection.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test that patches available_ram_bytes low enough (and/or sets a large per-profile memory limit via env) so a SINGLE heavy admission has reservation_bytes > (available - os_reserve) on an empty ledger, and assert it is still admitted (the per-context rss_limit_bytes is the real bound for one job). This becomes the RED test for V029; once fixed (`if reserved > 0 and reserved + reservation_bytes > limit_bytes:` or a clamp), it stays green.

findings.title: No test for the no-haute.toml deploy path where the raw --pipeline arg clobbers the resolved/discovered path (verified bug V005)
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V005: in handle_deploy's no-haute.toml branch (src/haute/cli/_deploy.py:118-124), the code first resolves the user-supplied pipeline argument via resolve_pipeline_file (which accepts a DIRECTORY and discovers the project pipeline inside, returning an absolute file path), then unconditionally overwrites it with the RAW unresolved CLI arg: `if config.pipeline_file: overrides['pipeline_file'] = Path(config.pipeline_file)`. So passing a directory as the pipeline argument breaks directory-discovery. The deploy CLI test file only exercises the haute.toml-present path (every test calls _make_toml(tmp_path)); there is no test for the no-toml branch at all, and no test passes a directory as the pipeline argument. The override-clobber regression is therefore entirely uncovered.
findings.evidence: Every TestDeploy method in test_cli_deploy.py calls `_make_toml(tmp_path)` (which writes haute.toml), so the `bounds/no-toml` branch at _deploy.py:118-124 is never entered. No test passes a directory to `haute deploy <dir>`.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test with NO haute.toml present that runs `haute deploy <project_dir>` (a directory containing a discoverable pipeline) and asserts the DeployConfig/resolve receives the discovered absolute file path, not the raw directory. As a RED test it reproduces V005 (resolution discarded); after the fix (make the override branch-aware) it passes.

findings.title: Windows RAM path test over-mocks and asserts only that GlobalMemoryStatusEx was called, never the value it returns
findings.description: available_ram_bytes is pricing-adjacent (it gates downsampling and in-flight admission). The Windows test fully mocks ctypes so the struct field ullAvailPhys is never populated, and the test explicitly notes 'we can't easily intercept field values'. Its only assertion is `mock_windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx.assert_called_once()`. It never asserts the returned byte count, the unit, or that the value is propagated — so a regression that called the API but returned a wrong/zero value (or ignored ullAvailPhys) would pass. This is a structure/'no exception + API called' assertion rather than a value assertion. The Linux/sysconf paths ARE value-checked (e.g. the 4 GiB fallback at lines 157-184), so this is a localized gap rather than a systemic one.
findings.evidence: test_ram_estimate.py:151-153 comment '...we can't easily intercept field values. Verify the API was called.' and line 155 `mock_windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx.assert_called_once()` is the sole assertion.
findings.recommended_fix: Drive the value through a fake: have the mocked GlobalMemoryStatusEx side_effect write a known ullAvailPhys into the passed struct (or refactor available_ram_bytes to read the field via an injectable seam) and assert available_ram_bytes() returns that exact byte count. That converts the test from 'API was called' to 'correct RAM value is returned', catching unit/field-mapping regressions.

findings.title: Disjunctive `== correct_value OR is None` assertions codify the evaluator's silent value-laundering as acceptable
findings.description: These trace-expression-evaluator tests assert the result with an OR-None escape hatch: `assert math.isnan(result.result_value) or result.result_value is None` (1194), `assert result.result_value == float('inf') or result.result_value is None` (1202), `assert result.result_value == float('-inf') or result.result_value is None` (1207). The correct single-row Polars value for `x*2` with x=inf is +inf, for `x+1` with x=-inf is -inf, and for `x+1` with x=NaN is NaN. The `or ... is None` clause makes the test PASS even when the evaluator silently returns None. None is exactly the laundered value produced by `evaluate_expression`'s top-level `except Exception` (src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1302-1304), which on ANY internal failure returns `row_values.get(target_column)` (None when the key is absent). So these assertions bless the precise silent-failure path that VERIFIED-BUGS catalog #23 (`except Exception` masks wrong numbers) and CLAUDE.md ("fail loudly ... a fallback which is incorrect and hard to notice") forbid. A genuine regression that broke inf/NaN handling inside the evaluator would not be caught.
findings.evidence: src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1302-1304: `try: return _evaluate_expression_impl(...) except Exception: parsed = parse_expression(...)` then EvaluatedExpression(..., result_value=row_values.get(target_column), ...) at line 1323. Catalog #23 repro `parser__expr-evaluator-catchall-masks-bugs.py` ran green proving a real ZeroDivisionError on `pl.col('a')/pl.col('b')` is laundered into the observed value with no log. The disjunctive asserts here accept that None outcome.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the exact correct value: `assert result.result_value == float('inf')` (and `-inf`, and `math.isnan(result.result_value)`). If the evaluator legitimately cannot represent a single-row inf/NaN, that is a design decision that should be asserted as an explicit error/marker, not silently permitted via `or is None`. Add a companion test that injects a real internal evaluator failure (e.g. division by zero) and asserts the trace surfaces an error/None-with-marker rather than echoing the observed value, per the catalog #23 fix.

findings.location: tests/test_trace.py (TestRowCorrelation* classes, ~145-374) and tests/test_trace_integration.py:1434-1572 (TestRowCorrelation* classes) — no test anywhere exercises a numeric trace value against a string parent column; `_build_value_match_expr` has zero direct coverage (grep across tests/ = no files)
findings.title: No test covers the dtype-asymmetric correlation crash (V027): a numeric value vs a string parent column aborts the entire trace
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V027 is a confirmed, still-live HIGH-area crash: `_build_value_match_expr` (src/haute/_trace_correlation.py:186-189) casts the COLUMN to Utf8 only when the match VALUE is a str; when the value is numeric and the parent column is Utf8 it emits bare `pl.col(column) == value`, which Polars rejects with ComputeError('cannot compare string with numeric type'). Symmetrically a NaN/inf value against a Utf8 column emits `is_nan()`/`is_infinite()`, raising InvalidOperationError. This runs inside `indexed.select(...)` on the trace.py post-hoc correlation path with NO try/except, so a perfectly ordinary graph (parent has a string code column; a child casts it to Int and filters rows so the same-row-count fast path is bypassed) makes the whole 'click a price to trace it' request hard-fail instead of degrading to the documented (None,-1). The entire row-correlation test surface only ever matches values whose dtype already agrees with the column (or shares the column name so casting is symmetric), so this critical crash is invisible to CI.
findings.evidence: I executed review/04-exhaustive/repro/V027.py against the current tree: '[A] numeric value vs string column RAISED ComputeError: cannot compare string with numeric type (i32)'; '[C] NaN value vs string column RAISED InvalidOperationError: is_nan operation not supported for dtype str'; '[D] _correlate_rows_posthoc RAISED ComputeError ... [(col("code")) == (dyn int: 20)].fill_null([false])'. Source still has the asymmetric guard at _trace_correlation.py:186-189. Grep for `_build_value_match_expr` in tests/ returns no files.
findings.recommended_fix: Add failing tests first (per CLAUDE.md TDD-for-bugs): (1) unit `_build_value_match_expr('x', 2)` against a Utf8 column and `_build_value_match_expr('s', float('nan'))` against a Utf8 column must NOT raise (assert a False/non-matching predicate); (2) end-to-end via execute_trace with a parent string column, a child that casts it to Int and filters rows (so the positional fast path is bypassed), asserting the trace returns with a no-match/ambiguity diagnostic rather than raising. Then make the comparison dtype-robust (compare stringwise, or wrap so an incompatible compare yields False) preserving the (None,-1) fail-soft.

findings.title: Reorder-correlation tests give false confidence: the dangerous rename+sort-with-no-shared-column case (V027/#27 positional fast-path misroute) is untested
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS catalog #27 confirms (executed repro, exit 1) that `_correlate_rows_posthoc` attaches the WRONG parent row when a same-row-count transform reorders rows and leaves NO column name shared between parent and child output (e.g. `df.select(pl.col('a').alias('b')).sort('b', descending=True)`): the `if not shared:` fast-path at _trace_correlation.py:637-643 accepts the positionally-aligned parent row, so the actuary sees a different policy's input as the contribution to the clicked price, silently. The test suite's `TestRowCorrelationSortChangesOrder` docstring explicitly claims 'Sort reorders rows; positional matching would give wrong results', but its body uses `df.sort('id')` where `id` is SHARED, so value-matching rescues it — it never exercises the no-shared-column path that actually triggers the bug. `test_positional_match_with_columns` likewise keeps the `x` column shared. The suite therefore advertises reorder-robustness it does not have.
findings.evidence: test_trace_integration.py:1551-1570 builds `_transform_node('sorted', "df = df.sort('id')")` with `id` present in both parent and child; the assertion `sorted_step.output_values['id'] == 1` passes via value-match. Catalog #27 repro `projection-trace__posthoc-positional-fastpath-reorder.py` (REPRODUCED, exit 1): parent a=[10,20,30], child b=[30,20,10] via `parent.select(pl.col('a').alias('b')).sort('b', descending=True)`; clicking child b==30 correlates to parent a==10 (positional row 0) instead of a==30. Control without the sort returns correct, isolating reorder as trigger.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a failing test mirroring the repro: source a=[10,20,30] -> transform `df.select(pl.col('a').alias('b')).sort('b', descending=True)`; trace child row 0 (b==30) and assert the correlated parent row is a==30 (true lineage) OR that the trace surfaces an 'unresolved/ambiguous' diagnostic — never the positional a==10. Then gate the `if not shared:` positional acceptance behind a proven row-order-preservation invariant (or a stable row-identity token).

findings.location: tests/test_trace_fail_loudly.py:195-489 (every test in TestItem3SilentEnrichmentExcepts and the parametrised smoke test) and :665-712
findings.title: Fail-loudly tests pass on ANY exception via `if exc is not None: return`, and only exercise injected raises — never the real silent value-laundering they were written to prevent
findings.description: Each test uses `_run_trace_loudly`, which catches ExecutionError and returns it; the test body then short-circuits with `if exc is not None: return` (lines 213-215, 251-252, 302-303, 383-384, 410-411, 471-472; and 695-698 for the waterfall test). This means the test passes if the trace raises ANY ExecutionError for ANY reason — including reasons unrelated to the injected failure — without ever checking the failure is the specific one under test. Worse, the suite proves fail-loudly only by monkeypatching helper functions (`parse_expression`, `evaluate_expression`, `build_waterfall`, ...) to raise `_BoomError` from OUTSIDE. The actual catalogued bugs (#23/#29/#47) are NOT raises: the real `evaluate_expression` swallows internal failures in its own `except Exception` (src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1302-1304) and returns the observed value, so it never raises and never sets a visible-failure field. These tests structurally cannot exercise that path because they force the raise externally; they validate the outer wrapper while the inner laundering remains uncaught. The file's own docstring asserts coverage of '15+ silent except Exception sites' but the real silent site (the inner catch-all) is untested.
findings.evidence: test_trace_fail_loudly.py:145-146 `_run_trace_loudly` returns `(None, exc, captured)` on ExecutionError; bodies then `if exc is not None: return` (e.g. 213-215). The injected failures all come via `monkeypatch.setattr('haute.trace.<fn>', _explodes)` (205, 243, 294, 375, 402, 463, 678). Catalog #23 repro shows the real inner `except Exception` at _expression_parser.py:1536-1539/1302-1325 launders ZeroDivisionError/TypeError into the observed value with NO raise and NO log — a path these tests never enter.
findings.recommended_fix: (1) On the `exc is not None` branch, assert the exception is the injected one (e.g. `isinstance(exc.__cause__, _BoomError)` or message contains the sentinel) instead of returning unconditionally. (2) Add tests that drive a REAL internal evaluator failure without monkeypatching the outer function — e.g. a construct that raises inside `_evaluate_expression_impl` (division by zero, `round` on a str) — and assert the trace surfaces an error/marker rather than `result_value == observed`. This is the regression the catalog #23 fix requires and that the current suite misses.

findings.location: tests/test_projection_planner.py (entire TestSingleParentPolars* family ~783-1755; no test references pl.sum/pl.mean/pl.min/pl.max/pl.first/pl.std/pl.n_unique with a string column argument)
findings.title: Projection planner has no test for string-argument Polars aggregation shortcuts that silently under-demand the parent (V007)
findings.description: VERIFIED-BUGS V007 (executed repro) confirms `_referenced_polars_columns` (src/haute/projection.py:789-802) returns an empty column set for top-level aggregation shortcuts that name a column by string argument — `pl.sum('a')`, `pl.mean('a')`, `pl.min/max/first/last/std/var/median/count/n_unique('a')` — instead of bailing to full width as the module's stated invariant requires (the dynamic `pl.col(...)` branch correctly returns None). Several of these are row-preserving inside `with_columns`, so the planner emits a NARROWED edge demand that omits the referenced column, under-demanding the parent. The projection planner suite is otherwise extremely thorough about `pl.col('a')` references, select/rename/filter, and derived columns, but contains zero coverage of the string-argument aggregation shortcuts, so this silent under-demand (which surfaces as ColumnNotFoundError, or a wrong narrowed scan at deploy if a same-named column exists) is untested on a pricing-critical strict-profile path.
findings.evidence: Grep of test_projection_planner.py for `pl.sum(`/`pl.mean(`/`pl.min(`/`pl.max(`/`pl.first(`/`pl.std(`/`pl.n_unique(` and 'under-demand' returns only union-walk commentary at lines 1658/1705-1706, none exercising the shortcuts. V007 repro is listed REPRODUCED in VERIFIED-BUGS (executed-repro). Source `_referenced_polars_columns` only special-cases `pl.col(...)` (projection.py:796-801).
findings.recommended_fix: Add planner tests for a single-parent polars node whose code is e.g. `df = df.with_columns(total=pl.sum('a'))` (and the other shortcuts) under LAZY_SINK, asserting the parent edge demand INCLUDES 'a' (or bails to full width / None), never an empty/narrowed set that drops it. Pair with the V007 production fix (return None for any `pl.<func>(...)` with a non-`pl.col` argument that cannot be proven column-free).

findings.location: tests/test_trace_waterfall.py:458-517 (TestPassthroughSteps) and tests/test_trace_coverage.py build_waterfall section (~644+); src/haute/_trace_waterfall.py:483 gate
findings.title: No test for the identity-for-this-row rating step silently dropped from the waterfall (catalog #56)
findings.description: build_waterfall_from_steps gates membership on `column in diff.columns_modified` (src/haute/_trace_waterfall.py:483), and `_compute_schema_diff` marks a column modified only if in_val != out_val on the single traced row (src/haute/_trace_correlation.py:155). A genuine multiplicative rating step that evaluates to factor 1.0 FOR THIS ROW (e.g. `when(region=='X').then(1.2).otherwise(1.0)` for a non-X row) leaves the cell unchanged, lands in columns_passed, and is silently omitted from the explanation — yet the cumulative still reconciles so no WaterfallReconciliationError fires (catalog #56, executed repro EXIT=0). The waterfall tests do cover TRUE passthrough exclusion (`test_passthrough_between_rating_steps_adds_no_entry` asserts an unrelated node is absent), but they never assert that a step which STRUCTURALLY targets the traced column but is identity-for-this-row is still represented (or deliberately excluded with a documented reason). The completeness gap is untested, so a fix or regression here would be unguarded.
findings.evidence: src/haute/_trace_waterfall.py:483 `elif column in diff.columns_modified:` — identity rows go to columns_passed (correlation.py:151-158), bypassing this branch. findings.title: Ctrl+Shift+Z redo test fires a physically-impossible {key:"z", shiftKey:true} event, making the permanently-broken redo shortcut (V079) pass
findings.description: The test `it("Ctrl+Shift+Z calls redo")` dispatches `new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "z", ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true })` and asserts `redo` is called. In a real browser, when Shift is physically held the `KeyboardEvent.key` for the Z key is the UPPERCASE "Z" (key reflects the produced character), never lowercase "z". The production handler at useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:54 checks `mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey` — a condition that can NEVER be true with a real Shift press (it would need key==="z" AND shift simultaneously). This is verified bug V079 ("Ctrl+Shift+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z redo is unreachable"). jsdom does not derive `key` from `shiftKey`; it uses the literal value passed, so the synthetic event satisfies the broken guard and the test goes green while the only macOS redo shortcut is dead. The test codifies the bug as intended behaviour and is exactly why CI did not catch V079.
findings.evidence: Test: `fireKey("z", { ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true }); expect(params.redo).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` with `fireKey = (key, opts) => window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key, bubbles: true, ...opts }))`. Production: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:54 `if (mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey && !isTyping) { ...; redo() }`. Catalog: V079 high-confidence executed-repro.
findings.recommended_fix: When the fix lands, the test must dispatch the realistic event `fireKey("Z", { ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true })` (uppercase key) — which fails against today's code and passes only once the handler normalises case (e.g. `e.key.toLowerCase() === "z"`). Add a sibling negative test asserting that `{ key: "z", shiftKey: true }` (the impossible combo) does NOT need handling, plus a Cmd+Shift+Z (metaKey) variant for macOS. The same uppercase-key realism must be applied to the TEXTAREA-ignore test at line 85-92 which has the identical defect.

findings.title: Every keyboard-shortcut test uses lowercase e.key, so CapsLock-breaks-all-letter-shortcuts (V080) is completely uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V080: all letter-key shortcuts (undo z, copy c, paste v, select-all a, group g, search k) silently break when CapsLock is on, because the handler compares `e.key` against lowercase literals with no case normalisation. With CapsLock on (and Shift off), the browser delivers `key: "Z"/"C"/"V"/...`. The entire 490-line test file only ever fires lowercase keys (`fireKey("z"...)`, `fireKey("c"...)`, etc.), so there is zero coverage of the uppercase code path. A user with CapsLock on loses every Ctrl shortcut and no test would notice.
findings.evidence: Handler: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:42,49,54,60,67 all use `e.key === "s"/"z"/"c"/"y"` literals; no `.toLowerCase()` anywhere. Tests only ever pass lowercase: e.g. lines 58,63,131,140,151,239,290. Catalog: V080 high-confidence code-trace.
findings.recommended_fix: After the handler normalises case, add a parametrised test that fires each shortcut with the uppercase key (CapsLock simulation: `{ key: "Z", ctrlKey: true }` with shiftKey false) and asserts the same action fires as the lowercase form. This pins V080 against regression.

findings.title: sanitizeName tests claim backend parity but never test a Python keyword, masking the missing keyword-prefix divergence (V091)
findings.description: Verified bug V091: the frontend `sanitizeName` omits the keyword-prefix step that the backend `_sanitize_func_name` performs, so a node labelled "class" (or def/return/import/lambda/etc.) sanitises to "class" on the frontend but "node_class" on the backend — a silent identifier divergence that breaks generated-code/round-trip parity. The test file explicitly documents itself as enforcing parity with the backend `_sanitize_func_name` (comment block at lines 65-70, and the non-ASCII `café -> caf_xe9_` cases) yet contains NO test for any Python keyword. It thoroughly tests spaces, hyphens, punctuation, leading digits, non-ASCII, CJK, emoji, and idempotency — giving the false impression of complete parity — but the one rule the implementation is actually missing is untested. Confirmed by source: sanitizeName.ts only prefixes when the result starts with a digit (line 36); there is no keyword check, and the docstring's 6-rule list omits keyword handling entirely.
findings.evidence: sanitizeName.ts:36 `if (name && /^[0-9]/.test(name)) name = ...` is the ONLY prefix step; no keyword set. Tests assert e.g. `sanitizeName("abc123")==="abc123"` but never `sanitizeName("class")`. Catalog: V091 high-confidence code-trace, backend ref `src/haute/_graph_utils.py _sanitize_func_name`.
findings.recommended_fix: Add failing tests `expect(sanitizeName("class")).toBe("node_class")`, `expect(sanitizeName("return")).toBe("node_return")`, and a non-keyword control `expect(sanitizeName("klass")).toBe("klass")`, mirroring the backend keyword set. Fix sanitizeName.ts to prefix Python keywords with `node_` (sharing the keyword list with, or kept in sync with, the backend), and update the docstring rule list. This is a high-value codifies-the-gap finding because the test's self-description asserts a parity it does not verify.

findings.title: detectGaps tests never exercise overlapping/nested rules, so the predecessor-upper (not running-max) bug (V073) is uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V073: `detectGaps` compares each sorted interval's upper bound against only its immediate predecessor's upper (`intervals[i].interval.upper`), not the running maximum upper seen so far. When rules overlap or nest (e.g. a wide rule [0,100] followed by a narrow nested rule [10,20] and then a far rule (>50)), the algorithm reports spurious or wrong gaps because a contained interval's small upper bound resets the comparison baseline. Every test in the detectGaps block uses cleanly ordered, non-overlapping intervals (simple gap, point gap, multiple gaps, open-ended). None feeds an overlapping or nested pair, which is precisely the input class that triggers the bug. detectOverlaps is separately tested for containment (line 122-129), so the data shapes were available — they were just never routed through detectGaps.
findings.evidence: bandingUtils.ts:146-157 loop uses `const curr = intervals[i].interval` (predecessor), not a running max. Tests at lines 163-209 only use disjoint sorted ranges. Catalog: V073 high-confidence code-trace.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test with a nested/overlapping set, e.g. rules [>=0,<=100], [>=10,<=20], [>50] and assert detectGaps returns [] (fully covered, no spurious gap). Add a second case where a genuine gap exists beyond an overlapping pair and assert only the real gap is reported. After fixing detectGaps to track running-max upper, these pin V073.

findings.title: OptimiserDataPreview's 600-line suite never feeds a non-finite series value, so the Chart-silently-coerces vs Statistics-throws divergence (V051) is untested
findings.description: Verified bug V051: the Chart tab silently coerces/drops non-finite (NaN/Infinity) series values (emitting e.g. an SVG path containing literal 'NaN' or dropping points), while the Statistics tab throws on the identical rows and trips the ErrorBoundary. This is an inconsistent failure mode across two tabs over the same data. The test suite is large and exercises chart rendering, series checkboxes, statistics means, navigation, and capping — but every `margin`/`volume` value in every fixture is a clean finite number. There is no test that places NaN or Infinity in a series and asserts how Chart and Statistics each behave. Because the two tabs diverge precisely on this input, the absence of any non-finite fixture means the bug is invisible to CI and the intended (consistent) behaviour is unspecified.
findings.evidence: All fixtures use finite values (e.g. margin: 100..240, volume: 0.86..1.0); the only 'extreme' value used is 1_000_000 (finite) at line 363. No NaN/Infinity anywhere in the file. Catalog: V051 high-confidence code-trace, `frontend/src/panels/OptimiserDataPreview.tsx:42-57`.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a fixture with `margin: Number.NaN` / `volume: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` and assert the decided contract on BOTH tabs: e.g. Chart path `d` strings contain no 'NaN'/'Infinity' (skip non-finite points like LossTab does) AND the Statistics tab renders without throwing (non-finite excluded from aggregates or shown as an explicit marker). Mirror the LossTab pattern (LossTab.test.tsx:18-53) which already does this for loss curves.

findings.title: LossChart has no non-finite path-coordinate test, unlike its sibling LossTab, leaving V089 (makePath emits 'NaN' coordinates) uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V089: `LossChart.makePath` filters points only with `e[key] != null` (LossChart.tsx:42), so a NaN/Infinity loss value yields an invalid SVG path segment like `L12.3,NaN`. The sibling component LossTab guards with a finite check and is explicitly tested for it (LossTab.test.tsx:18 "renders a valid loss curve without NaN or Infinity path coordinates" and the empty-state test at line 38). LossChart shares the identical logic (its own header comment says so) but its test file only ever uses clean finite data and never asserts the absence of 'NaN'/'Infinity' in path output. This is asymmetric coverage: the fix/guard was applied and pinned in LossTab but LossChart remains unguarded and untested. Note: catalog records that the related y-range-poisoning premise was refuted because backend `_assert_json_finite` guards loss_history, which lowers real-world reachability — hence medium/medium rather than high — but the per-point makePath defect (V089) was still verified by code-trace and the coverage gap versus the sibling is genuine.
findings.evidence: LossChart.tsx:42 `.map((e,i) => e[key] != null ? ... : null)` (null-only filter). LossTab.tsx guards with isFiniteNumber (per catalog V089) and is tested. LossChart.test.tsx uses only finite fixtures (lines 22-25, 37-41, 49-53). Catalog: V089 verified TS bug.
findings.recommended_fix: Port LossTab's non-finite test to LossChart: render with a loss_history containing `eval_rmse: Number.NaN` and `train_rmse: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` and assert no path `d` attribute matches /NaN|Infinity/. Fix LossChart.makePath to skip non-finite points (`isFiniteNumber(e[key])`) consistent with LossTab.

findings.title: FeatureImportance bar-width tests never use a negative or zero first importance, so the maxVal = items[0].importance bug (V090) is uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V090: `maxVal = items[0]?.importance || 1` (FeatureImportance.tsx:28) assumes the first item holds the maximum importance and is positive. Bar width is `(Math.abs(fi.importance)/Math.abs(maxVal))*100%`. For SHAP/permutation importances that can be negative or zero, or any list not sorted descending by magnitude, this denominator is wrong: bars overflow past 100% (when a later |importance| exceeds |items[0]|) or divide by an effectively wrong base. The test 'shows max 10 features' constructs importances `15 - i` (strictly positive, descending), so items[0] always equals the true max — the one arrangement that hides the bug. No test uses a negative importance, a zero first importance, or an unsorted list. The tests assert feature names render but never assert any computed bar width, so the value logic is entirely unverified.
findings.evidence: FeatureImportance.tsx:28 `const maxVal = items[0]?.importance || 1`; width at line 60. Test fixture line 78-81 uses `importance: 15 - i` (always positive descending). No assertion on the rendered `width` style anywhere. Catalog: V090 verified code-trace.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test with importances like `[{feature:'a',importance:2},{feature:'b',importance:-9}]` and assert that the rendered bar widths are clamped to <=100% / scaled by the max magnitude (b should be the full-width bar, a ~22%). After fixing maxVal to `Math.max(...items.map(i=>Math.abs(i.importance)))`, this pins V090. Also add a zero-first-value case to exercise the `|| 1` fallback path intentionally.

findings.title: removeFactor test only asserts terms is updated, never that orphaned interaction references are cleaned, hiding V064
findings.description: Verified bug V064: `removeFactor()` (GLMFactorConfig.tsx:134-137) deletes a column from `terms` only, never from `interactions`. Any interaction row referencing the removed factor is left dangling, the dropdown then shows a value not in its option list, and the stale name is persisted and sent to the backend where it flips `include_main` semantics. The test 'clicking remove on a factor removes it from terms' asserts only the `terms` onUpdate payload. There is no test that adds an interaction referencing a factor and then removes that factor while asserting the interaction is pruned (or the stale reference cleared). The incomplete assertion makes the buggy partial-removal behaviour look correct.
findings.evidence: Test asserts `expect(baseProps.onUpdate).toHaveBeenCalledWith("terms", {...})` only (lines 313-316); no interactions assertion. GLMFactorConfig.tsx:134-137 removeFactor mutates terms only. Catalog: V064 high-confidence executed-repro.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test: render with `terms: {age, region}` and `interactions: [{factors:['age','region'], include_main:true}]`, click 'Remove age', and assert onUpdate is called for BOTH `terms` (age gone) AND `interactions` (the orphaned row removed or 'age' cleared). After fixing removeFactor to also prune interactions, this pins V064.

findings.title: Paired-key tests never clear a key to empty, so the independent left/right normalisation producing unequal-length arrays (V060) is uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V060: `updatePairedKey` (EdgeJoinEditor.tsx:113-117) normalises `leftOn` and `rightOn` INDEPENDENTLY via `normalizeKeyRows`, which trims trailing empty entries. If a user clears one side of the only pair to '' while the other side is non-empty, `normalizeKeyRows(["a"]) === ["a"]` but `normalizeKeyRows([""]) === []`, persisting leftOn length 1 / rightOn length 0 — unequal-length arrays the backend rejects. The test 'updates paired key rows and can add another pair' only ever sets a key to a non-empty value ('region') and adds a pair; it never clears a key to empty, which is the exact trigger. The asymmetric-normalisation path is therefore untested.
findings.evidence: EdgeJoinEditor.tsx:116 `onUpdate({ on: [], leftOn: normalizeKeyRows(nextLeft), rightOn: normalizeKeyRows(nextRight) })` (independent trims); normalizeKeyRows trims trailing '' (lines 534+). Test only sets value 'region' (line 218) and adds a pair (line 225). Catalog: V060 high-confidence executed-repro.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test: render with `leftOn:['policy_id'], rightOn:['lookup_policy_id']`, change 'Join key 1' (right side) to '' and assert the persisted onUpdate keeps leftOn and rightOn the SAME length (either both length 1 with '' preserved, or both trimmed together). After fixing updatePairedKey to normalise the pair atomically (trim a row only when BOTH sides are empty), this pins V060.

findings.title: useMlflowBrowser tests never simulate out-of-order async resolution, so the stale-response race (V082) is uncovered
findings.description: Verified bug V082: out-of-order getRuns/getModelVersions resolutions can overwrite current data (refreshRuns/refreshVersions have no request-sequence/staleness guard). The hook tests mock the API with `mockResolvedValue` (resolves immediately, in call order) and only assert call counts and final arrays for sequential, in-order resolutions. None of the tests make an earlier call resolve AFTER a later call (e.g. a slow exp-1 fetch resolving after a fast exp-2 fetch) to prove the newer result is not clobbered. So the race condition is not pinned.
findings.evidence: Tests use `mockGetRuns.mockResolvedValue(fakeRuns)` and assert `runs` equals the single fixture; no deferred-promise ordering test. Catalog: V082 high-confidence code-trace, `useMlflowBrowser.ts:112-121,133-144`.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test using deferred promises: trigger refreshRuns('exp-1') (slow), then refreshRuns('exp-2') (fast), resolve exp-2 then exp-1, and assert `runs` reflects exp-2 (the latest request) — failing today, passing after a request-id/AbortController guard. Same shape for refreshVersions.

results.coverage_note: Reviewed the frontend vitest suite focusing on tests that pin confirmed bugs from VERIFIED-BUGS.md (V051,V060,V064,V068,V070,V073,V079,V080,V082,V089,V090,V091) and the frontend entries in catalog.md. Read in full: useKeyboardShortcuts.test.ts (+ KeyboardShortcuts modal test), sanitizeName.test.ts (+ source), bandingUtils.test.ts (+ source), LossChart.test.tsx + LossTab.test.tsx (+ LossChart.tsx source), FeatureImportance.test.tsx (+ source), useMlflowBrowser.test.ts, OptimiserDataPreview.test.tsx, EdgeJoinEditor.test.tsx (+ source updatePairedKey/normalizeKeyRows), GLMComponents.test.tsx (GLMFactorConfig section), useJobPolling.dedup.test.ts (header + unmount block), previewCache.test.ts (header). Verified the production sources for V079 (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:54), V089/V090 (LossChart.tsx:42 / FeatureImportance.tsx:28), V091 (sanitizeName.ts:36), V073 (bandingUtils.ts:146-157), V060 (EdgeJoinEditor.tsx:113-117,534). The standout is a genuine codifies-bug: useKeyboardShortcuts.test.ts dispatches an impossible {key:\"z\",shiftKey:true} event that makes the dead V079 redo shortcut pass (and is why CI missed it). The dominant pattern across this area is missing critical-path coverage where verified bugs live exactly in the untested input class (non-finite values, negative importances, Python keywords, overlapping banding rules, cleared join keys, orphaned interactions, CapsLock/uppercase keys) while suites otherwise test only clean/in-order/positive data. I did not find tests that assert numerically wrong values; the failure mode here is omission, plus the one unrealistic-event codification. Did NOT exhaustively read every one of the ~150 frontend test files (e.g. App.integration, useWebSocketSync.*, usePipelineAPI.*, store tests) — those were sampled via Grep for the specific bug signatures and not deeply audited line-by-line; a follow-up pass could cover V053/V055/V056/V061/V067/V068/V072/V074/V075/V076/V077/V081/V083/V084/V086 test surfaces in the same way. Confidence on each finding reflects whether I confirmed the production source defect directly (high) or inferred coverage absence from the test fixtures alone (medium/low).
